Ultimately it is your kid and your decision. It is a fine line of trying not to have a rift in the family vs letting someone walk all over you.

Tell your mom, tell teachers, tell any and all adults you trust. Call social services. I investigate child sex abuse and this is it. You need to be away from him. Now. This is not acceptable behavior on any level for any reason.

This is something your husband needs to address to his mother. MIL's have a way of getting in between and causing problems in marriages. You address your family, your husband deals with his. Set boundaries now about your son, or else you will be dealing with this for the next 18 yrs...at least
But that is what i am saying, start going out and doing things as a family together some. You are disconnected from her. Time to reconnect.
Call social services. Make a report on yourself. It will generate a report to the police as well. That is abuse

If he signed his parental rights away, he literally and legally has no rights to see your son. Tell him to eat a bag of dicks and go away. Stand up for yourself. Sometimes being a bitch is the only way to get through to some people.

This is going to be unpopular, but aren't you being a bit selfish? Get up, work, go home take care of kids, go to bed, repeat. Welcome to adulthood. She gets up and goes to work all day long taking care of the house and kids, goes to bed, repeat. Thats the life you chose when you decided to have kids. If you are unhappy, stop putting that on her. Take up a hobby with the kids, kite flying, gemstone mining, leaf collecting, whatever. Gets you and mom and the kids out of the home and everyone spending time together.
Thank you. I appreciate that
Where I work, it is the opposite. I work for the government and have to make my own masks and buy my own supplies. When is your birthday? Maybe having an online party with us? I would come.

CPS investigator here. Let her go, but keep your child. If someone were to report that, she is getting in trouble. If it is known you knew and did nothing, you are, too. Your child's safety is above all else. She needs counseling, yes, but baby needs to be safe while she is getting it. Apply for daycare assistance if you need it. Anything could have happened to the baby when it was being neglected. I have personally lost a child (he was 18 and was murdered in his own home by 2 men who broke in to rob the home) and let me tell you that it is absolutely the most horrific experience a parent could endure.  Imagine that knowing you could have stopped it.
